title: This Lake Is Inches Deep Yet Mirrors the Whole Sky — QG Loop P3 | China Travel Expert
description:
A lake so shallow you can walk across it — and so still it mirrors the entire sky. This is stop three on the Qinghai–Gansu Loop.

Chaka Salt Lake sits at about 3,100m in eastern Qinghai, roughly 150km southwest of Qinghai Lake (our last stop). Its Tibetan name simply means "salt lake." In summer the water lies just inches deep over a hard, near-pure salt crust, turning the whole surface into a natural mirror — which is why it's called the "Mirror of the Sky." It's also China's first green edible-salt production base. The reflection is best in the early morning, before the wind picks up and ripples the glass.

🧭 Expert Tip: Arrive before 9am. The mirror is perfect only when the air is dead still; by noon the wind breaks it into ordinary water. Take your time here — it's worth building the whole day around this one stop.

This is Part 3 of the Qinghai–Gansu Loop, told stop by stop. The full route guide lives on the channel page.
